routing_warnings.description: The client asks for the app code as part of the missing codebase delivery; this does not report mobile-application runtime behavior.
The client cannot locate the Flutter source code, which concerns source-code delivery rather than an executed failure of the mobile application.
The freelancer claims the requested Flutter code is in the repository, addressing its delivery location.
The freelancer identifies the frontend folder as the Flutter code location, continuing the source-delivery claim.
The missing-file clause concerns source-code delivery; the same message provides no executed mobile-app result because the client explicitly says it was not tested.
The statement that the project is not live concerns deployment rather than the mobile application's runtime behavior.
This message specifically reports exposed APIs and paths, which is better routed to the API endpoint protection Requirement.
This message requests replacement of exposed API endpoints rather than a change to repository visibility.
The message reports that the backend is not deployed, which concerns the live server deployment rather than source-code delivery.
The message concerns the repository being public rather than delivery of the source code.
The reported online exposure concerns repository privacy rather than source-code delivery.
The message concerns exposed API paths and endpoints rather than source-code delivery.
The request for deployment steps in a file belongs to the separate deployment-guide deliverable.
The step-by-step deployment-document request belongs to the deployment-guide Requirement.
The question about missing Flutter hybrid code concerns the mobile application rather than live server deployment.
The Play Store and App Store portion of this message belongs to the mobile-store publication Requirement.
